name: Kievan Rus'

areaKm2.note: Wikipedia infobox gives 1,330,000 km2 (c. 1000). The world_1000 polygon measures 1.20 million km2. Low allows for the sparse forest north-east being only nominally ruled.

population.note: Infobox: 5.4 million in 1000 (Urlanis, Rost naseleniya v Evrope). HYDE/OWID 1000-1100 series for Ukraine (0.9-1.4M), Belarus (0.2-0.3M) and European Russia (~60% of 2.5-3.8M) sum to ~3-4M (low). Mid 5.5M with modest growth to 1050.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Kiev ~36,000-50,000 by 1200 and Novgorod 10,000-15,000 in 1000 (Martin 2004, via the Kievan Rus' article); many small gorods.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Standing element: the druzhinas of Yaroslav and his sons in the appanages plus hired Varangians. Ibrahim ibn Yaqub gave Mieszko I of Poland a paid druzhina of 3,000 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Druzhina), a comparable neighbour. audit 2026-10-30: date basis: a year without a general muster, so only the household element is active and campaign levies are trainedReserves (france-1415, dated to the Agincourt campaign, counts its assembled army instead).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Town militias (voi) of Kiev, Novgorod, Chernigov and other gorods, and allied Torks and Pecheneg remnants. Franklin and Shepard (The Emergence of Rus 750-1200) give no total.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Boat crews and household officials.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Free townsmen and some peasants could be called for defence.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Princely druzhina: mail, conical helm, lance, sword.
Educated guess. Varangian mercenaries and town core troops on pay.
Educated guess. Archers in princely service.
Educated guess. Steppe auxiliaries (Torks) and mounted scouts.
Educated guess. Monoxyla river boats (each ~40 men) used for the 1043 sea raid on Constantinople, which ended in disaster.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: dugout-based boats vs Byzantine galleys and Greek fire.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: Yaroslav crushed the Pechenegs at Kiev (1036) but lost the 1043 naval expedition.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: appanage system and princely rivalry; druzhinas loyal to their own prince.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: confident state at its height under Yaroslav.

weapons.note: Anchor 3-4: sword, lance, composite bow, axe; no crossbow in quantity.

ships.note: Anchor 2: oared river boats (monoxyla) able to reach the Black Sea.

fortification.note: Anchor 2-3: timber walls on earth ramparts, the Serpent's Wall frontier ramparts, stone Golden Gate of Kiev (1037).

logistics.note: Anchor 2-3: river transport, winter sledges, portages.

isr.note: Anchor 2-3: steppe watch posts on the southern frontier.

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess. Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID) Poland 1400 = 956, Turkey 1000 = 768 (2011 int$); river trade wealth concentrated in towns.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Tribute (poliudie) supported the druzhina.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Town crafts, iron working.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Black-earth south vs poor forest north.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. No engineered roads; rivers in summer, frozen rivers and sledges in winter.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Kiev, Novgorod, Staraya Ladoga, Smolensk and Tmutarakan.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. River boats of the Varangians-to-Greeks route.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pre-modern armies with carts and pack animals operated ~1-2 weeks' march from a depot or navigable water.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses and oxen, ~0.1 per inhabitant.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.3: forest and marsh depth and harsh winter against steppe and southern invaders; less against northern neighbours, so mid 1.25.

notes: Snapshot = 1050, near the end of Yaroslav the Wise's reign (died 1054) and before the appanage strife. Army sizes are educated guesses: no modern total for Rus' forces exists in the works consulted, and Primary Chronicle numbers are not used. Population convention: all lands under Rurikid princes, including Novgorod and Tmutarakan; Polotsk counted although its prince was semi-independent. Per the feudal-host convention activePersonnel is the druzhinas only and the town militias are trainedReserves.
